pr_title: Make DSA.Create, AesCcm, AesGcm, ChaCha20Poly1305 throw PNSE on iOS
pr_body:
Fixes #52758
Fixes #51332
Fixes #51331
Fixes #51330
Fixes #51370

This PR re-enables all System.Security.Cryptography.* tests to ensure sufficient coverage of the change.

review_comments:
I think we generally omit `maccatalyst` when there is already `ios` exclusion

/cc @steveisok

I was under the impression that they just were not added yet. They are certainly present on some places and not on others.

I'm bit worried about any potential asymmetry of the APIs. For example, it's fine to build the libraries with `net6.0-ios` target and it gets consumed by Mac Catalyst through fallback. However, if I do some runtime check with `OperatingSystem.IsIOS()` I also have to explicitly test for `IsMacCatalyst` (and `IsTvOS`) because there's no fallback there. I mentally map the `UnsupportedOSPlatform` declarations to the `OperatingSystem` APIs (which is how the platform analyzer maps the code branches) so I expect there to be symmetry of both of requiring explicit Mac Catalyst declaration/check.
@MaximLipnin is looking at how the analyzer behaves for Catalyst because I'm not totally sure if we will get the same thing as ios.

As far as I can tell the [Platform Compatibility Analyzer](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/tree/main/src/NetAnalyzers/Core/Microsoft.NetCore.Analyzers/InteropServices) has no special case for Mac Catalyst. Hence it maintains the symmetry between `OperatingSystem.IsXXX` APIs and `UnsupportedOSPlatform("xxx")`. `OperatingSystem.IsIOS()` returns `false` on Mac Catalyst.

Based on what I've got from building the net6-mobile-samples using the latest SDK, the platform compatibility analyzer doesn't consider iOS as a superset for MacCatalyst, so it makes sense to use a separate `UnsupportedOSPlatform("maccatalyst")]` annotation.
Thanks for double checking my assumption!
